title: Ops Utility Orchestration & Runbooks-as-First-Class-Tasks
creator: Marcus Li
description: Problem: On-call engineers and operators still rely on a mix of ad-hoc scripts, Google Drive runbooks, and one-off Slack snippets to perform common admin tasks (user onboarding, key rotation, emergency throttling, tenant resets). This leads to inconsistent outcomes, high cognitive load during incidents, and difficulty automating recurring maintenance. Goal: Deliver an ops utility orchestration layer that treats runbooks as first-class Linear tasks and exposes a safe, auditable set of admin primitives that can be executed from the Console, admin CLI, and Slack. This ticket: build the initial orchestration service, a templating UX for runbook-to-task translation, and the first automated flows (tenant-lockdown, API-key rotation, cache priming).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible orchestration service (ops-hub) deployed to staging with documented service contract (HTTP API + JWT auth)
Three canonical runbooks converted into executable task templates (tenant-lockdown, api-key-rotate, cold-cache-warmup) with parameter validation and dry-run mode
Linear task creation triggered by template execution; tasks carry links to runbook source and include execution metadata (actor, params, run_id)
Slack slash command (/ops) that can launch a dry-run and then, with 2FA approval, run the tenant-lockdown flow; audit events visible in Console logs
End-to-end tests covering happy path and failure modes; postmortem playbook exercised in a simulated outage and completed without manual adhoc steps
implementation_plan: MVP orchestration service (ops-hub): HTTP API, template registry, execution engine, event log (append-only)
Create a runbook template DSL (YAML-based) with required/optional params, validation, and step types (http, kubectl, sql, sdk)
CLI extension (adminctl ops) to list templates, run dry-run, and execute with confirmation; emits Linear task link when executed
Slack integration: slash command + ephemeral confirm modal; wire 2FA/approval flow via SSO session check
DB schema for execution metadata and audit logs; retention policy and export to S3 for compliance
Instrumentation: metrics for execution success, latency, and number of manual interventions; Console dashboard for ops-hub
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental destructive actions run by mistake -> Mitigation: strict safe-mode defaults, required param confirmation, and 2-step approvals for destructive templates
Risk: secrets leaking in logs -> Mitigation: redact secrets at producer level, use parameter masks, and integrate KMS for transient credentials
Risk: template drift vs source-of-truth runbooks -> Mitigation: include source link in template metadata and add a weekly mismatch report (templates vs Drive docs)
Risk: too many one-off templates -> Mitigation: introduce template review process; templates require PM or SRE approval before production enablement

notes: We intentionally separate runbook content (Drive/Confluence) from executable templates to maintain human-readable guidance while enabling automation.
Future work (post-MVP): RBAC for template execution per-org, scheduled maintenance flows, and integration with incident timelines for automatic task creation.
Consider exporting completed executions to a standardized incident timeline format (OT-JSON) for audit and compliance teams.
